Who wrote them, and how they were sung
English churches sang the psalms in metre for over a century before Watts. These hymn books changed that, and were sung in a way that would surprise us now.
1773 · Amazing grace. Newton writes it for the New Year's Day service of 1773, on David's prayer in 1 Chronicles 17. That same month Cowper falls into a long darkness.
Independent minister in London; never strong in health, he wrote most of his hymns for his own congregation to sing after the sermon.
Sailor, slave-ship captain, then Anglican curate. Later rector in London, he spoke against the slave trade in print in 1788.
One of the finest poets of his day, and often in deep despair. His hymns hold both the trust and the dark.
Hymn books printed only the words. Tunes lived in separate tune books, or in the clerk's head.
Few could read and books were dear, so a clerk read or sang each line and the congregation sang it back after him.
Common Metre (8.6.8.6) is the old ballad measure. A Common Metre text fits any Common Metre tune, which is why our pages give a metre and not a tune.
Olney Hymns were written for a weekday meeting in a large room, not for Sunday worship, where the metrical psalms still ruled.
Search by first line, subject or passage, or narrow by hymn book, part of the Bible and metre. A card opens the hymn.
